title: Adrenal crisis
subject: endocrinology
summary: Suspect in anyone with adrenal insufficiency or current or recent glucocorticoid use who has unexplained shock, vomiting or collapse; give hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or IM at once, 1 L saline in the first hour, then 200 mg/24 hours, and prevent recurrence with sick-day rules and an emergency card.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Hypotension or hypovolaemic shock (often out of proportion to the trigger and resistant to fluids and vasopressors) plus one or more of: nausea or vomiting, severe fatigue, fever, abdominal pain, impaired consciousness (confusion, somnolence, collapse, seizures).

Who is at risk: known primary or secondary adrenal insufficiency, and anyone on or recently off glucocorticoids by any route (oral, inhaled, topical, intra-articular, injected), including undeclared steroid use.
Supportive labs (not needed for diagnosis): hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia (primary adrenal insufficiency), raised urea and creatinine, hypoglycaemia, eosinophilia, lymphocytosis.

Triggers: infection (gastroenteritis, urinary, respiratory, sepsis), surgery, trauma, labour, dental procedures, missed doses, abrupt steroid withdrawal or taper below physiological dose, and strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital).
Higher risk: previous crisis, age over 65, adolescence, multiple comorbidities. In India, adrenal tuberculosis is an important cause of new primary adrenal insufficiency.

sections.title: Immediate treatment
items: Do not delay treatment for tests. If it causes no delay, draw blood for cortisol and ACTH (plus renin and aldosterone if possible) before the first dose.
Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV (or IM if no access) immediately.
0.9% saline 1 L IV within the first hour, then continuous isotonic saline guided by haemodynamics; smaller boluses in heart failure or the elderly. Treat hypoglycaemia with IV glucose.
Then hydrocortisone 200 mg/24 hours, preferably as a continuous IV infusion, or 50 mg IV or IM every 6 hours, until clinical recovery; consider higher doses in very high body weight.
If hydrocortisone is unavailable, use prednisolone; dexamethasone is the least preferred alternative (no mineralocorticoid effect).
Find and treat the trigger (for example antibiotics for infection). Admit; ICU if shock persists after hydrocortisone and fluids.
Treat even if the diagnosis is uncertain: short courses of stress-dose hydrocortisone are safe.

sections.title: Monitoring and step-down
items: Monitor BP, heart rate, urine output, sodium, potassium and glucose closely; correct hyponatraemia at a controlled rate and watch for fluid overload.
When improving, reduce hydrocortisone (for example to 100 mg/day the next day) and taper to oral dosing once eating and stable.
Then give double the usual oral dose for about 48 hours (for example hydrocortisone 40 mg/day as 20 mg on rising, 10 mg at midday and 10 mg at 5 pm) before returning to maintenance.

Maintenance: hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses (or prednisolone 4 to 6 mg/day); in primary adrenal insufficiency add fludrocortisone 50 to 100 mcg/day once hydrocortisone is below stress doses.
Refer to endocrinology to confirm the cause (ACTH, renin, adrenal antibodies, adrenal imaging for tuberculosis, haemorrhage or metastases) and plan education.

sections.title: Sick-day rules and stress dosing
items: Minor illness (fever, bed rest, antibiotics): raise hydrocortisone to 40 mg/day in three doses (20, 10, 10 mg) or prednisolone to 10 mg/day for 2 to 5 days or the antibiotic course. Not needed if already on at least these doses, unless unstable.
Vomiting or diarrhoea: hydrocortisone 100 mg IM immediately, repeated after 6 hours if needed; go to hospital if symptoms continue or the patient is unwell.

Surgery under general or regional anaesthesia, and labour: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV at induction or onset of labour, then 200 mg/24 hours infusion (or 50 mg IV every 6 hours); after uncomplicated surgery give double oral dose for 48 hours.
Procedures under local anaesthesia: oral hydrocortisone 40 mg that day (20 mg 1 hour before, 10 mg 6 hours after, 10 mg 6 hours later).
Everyone at risk needs a steroid emergency card, medical alert ID and a hydrocortisone 100 mg injection kit, with training for the patient and family.
Patients on or recently off glucocorticoids who have not had HPA axis recovery confirmed need the same stress-dose cover.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Children: hydrocortisone 50 mg/m2 IV or IM immediately, then 50 to 100 mg/m2 per 24 hours, with fluid resuscitation; use a paediatric protocol.
Glucocorticoid taper: once on a physiological dose, a morning (8 to 9 am) cortisol above 300 nmol/L (10 mcg/dL), measured at least 24 hours after the last dose, indicates HPA axis recovery.
Coexisting hypothyroidism: start hydrocortisone before levothyroxine, as thyroid hormone can precipitate crisis.
Starting rifampicin (for example for tuberculosis) or another strong CYP3A4 inducer increases glucocorticoid clearance: review, and usually increase, the glucocorticoid dose.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for cortisol results or a Synacthen test before giving hydrocortisone.
Not considering adrenal insufficiency in patients on inhaled, topical or intra-articular steroids, or in the months after stopping steroids.
Stopping long-term steroids abruptly, or not increasing the dose during illness or surgery.
Using dexamethasone first-line when hydrocortisone is available.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone (crisis)
drugs.dose: 100 mg IV or IM immediately, then 200 mg/24 hours by continuous IV infusion or 50 mg IV or IM every 6 hours
drugs.notes: Children: 50 mg/m2 then 50 to 100 mg/m2 per 24 hours. Taper once recovering.

drugs.name: 0.9% sodium chloride
drugs.dose: 1 L IV within the first hour, then continuous infusion guided by haemodynamics
drugs.notes: Smaller boluses in heart failure and older adults.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone (oral stress dose)
drugs.dose: 40 mg/day in three doses (20 mg on rising, 10 mg midday, 10 mg 5 pm) for 2 to 5 days of minor illness

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone (emergency IM, self or carer)
drugs.dose: 100 mg IM, repeat after 6 hours if needed
drugs.notes: For vomiting, diarrhoea or inability to take tablets; then seek hospital care.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone (maintenance)
drugs.dose: 15 to 25 mg/day orally in 2 or 3 divided doses
drugs.notes: Prednisolone 4 to 6 mg/day is the physiological equivalent.

drugs.name: Fludrocortisone
drugs.dose: 50 to 100 mcg orally once daily (starting dose)
drugs.notes: Primary adrenal insufficiency only; not needed during high-dose hydrocortisone.
